throughput_regression.interpretation: Halving bytes should have given ~0.5x on a purely bandwidth-bound kernel; observed 0.73x in the >=10k bucket, and effective GB/s fell ~30%. The F16C conversion plus the unchanged per-dimension FMA count, not bytes, is now the limiter.
throughput_regression.caveat: effective GB/s uses scope_card*bytes_per_candidate, an estimate of bytes touched, not a hardware counter

op_budget_estimate.caveat: 3 ops/cycle assumes two FMA-capable ports and perfect scheduling; a real 8-accumulator unroll will land below this ideal

known_regressions: small scopes 1.8-2.3x slower from per-call vector allocation and 18-element sort; absolute cost ~1.1 ms of 240 ms

next_candidates_ranked.idea: reduce ops per candidate: 8 accumulators, hoist the cutoff test out of the inner 4-dim block, avoid per-call allocations
next_candidates_ranked.why: compute is now the wall; no new data structure needed

next_candidates_ranked.idea: product-quantized ADC (m=64) with per-vector error bound for exactness
next_candidates_ranked.why: cuts both bytes (64 B) and ops (64 lookups) per candidate
next_candidates_ranked.risk: high: codebook training cost, bound tightness unmeasured

next_candidates_ranked.idea: per-lane early rejection instead of tile-wide rejection
next_candidates_ranked.why: tile-wide reject needs all 8 lanes worse, which is rare in mixed tiles
next_candidates_ranked.risk: medium: adds a mask op per accumulate

not_claimed: no new recall or memory claim; run14 variance is tail-driven, so the 0.82 ms figure should be read with the 0.69-0.85 ms repeat range
